text: If a triangle has two angles equal to one another then the sides subtending the equal angles will also be equal to one another. Let $ABC$ be a triangle having the angle $ABC$ equal to the angle $ACB$. I say that side $AB$ is also equal to side $AC$.
For if $AB$ is unequal to $AC$ then one of them is greater.
assertion: one of AB, AC is greater than the other

text: And let $DB$, equal to the lesser $AC$, have been cut off from the greater $AB$ [Prop.~1.3].
Therefore, since $DB$ is equal to $AC$, and $BC$ (is) common, the two sides $DB$, $BC$ are equal to the two sides $AC$, $CB$, respectively,
assertion: the two sides DB, BC equal the two sides AC, CB respectively

text: and the angle $DBC$ is equal to the angle $ACB$.

text: Thus, if a triangle has two angles equal to one another then the sides subtending the equal angles will also be equal to one another. (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
